outcomes: A consumer reads which services a build serves from one strictly parsed document and refuses the whole document when any part of it is invalid
The same services give the same bytes and the same digest whatever their registration order
A Connect service is found in the HTTP route inventory of the same build through the route its source kind names
nonGoals: Message types, request and response schemas or protobuf descriptors
Listener addresses, ports, TLS settings or any environment value
Reachability and visibility, which the HTTP route inventory owns
Which surfaces a framework composes and when it describes them, which the producer's own feature owns

requirements.text: The protocol identifier is putnami.grpc-services.v1 and the schema URL is https://putnami.dev/schemas/putnami-grpc-services-v1.json. The published schema carries that $id and pins that $schema and that protocol. Its members match the Go types of the manifest, a service, a method and a provenance, and its transport and sourceKind enums match the Go values.

An inventory parses strictly and fails as a whole: an invalid one returns no manifest. Each of the 29 invalid fixtures fails with its expected code, among them an unknown member, trailing JSON, a missing services, methodsKnown or streaming flag, another protocol or schema and a wrong digest. Both valid fixtures validate, and every expected code is registered. The Go extension checks an inventory its describe wrote or staged with this parser, refuses a malformed one with its code and passes a canonical one.

A service name is dot-joined identifier segments, one segment included; an empty name or a leading dot is invalid. A Connect basePath ends in /<name>/ behind a mount prefix with no empty, dot or percent-escaped segment. A connect-gateway source on grpc is a mismatch. Name, transport and basePath identify a service: one name on two transports or base paths is valid, and a repeated triple is a duplicate even when byte-identical. The Go gRPC plugins collapse an identical registration and fail on a conflict.

Canonicalization gives one byte form and one digest: the full fixture yields the committed golden and its pinned digest, also with its services and methods reversed, on each of 100 runs, and leaves the input unchanged. A nil or empty inventory yields the minimal fixture and its pinned digest, a service without methods serializes an empty methods list and round-trips, and a nil manifest or a manifest of another protocol is refused.

A grpc-server service has no basePath and lists every registered method with its streaming flags, as the Go gRPC server does for health and enabled reflection. A connect-gateway service lists no method and joins one prefix route at its basePath that admits POST, under the route inventory's project, as the Go gateway does with and without a path prefix. An api-bridge service lists its methods, each joined by one exact POST route at basePath plus its name, as the Go API bridge does.
